_doc: HUMAN-AUTHORED. Demo scaffolding standing in for a review UI.
We permit simulating human overrides. Rather than inventing them,
most of what this system replays comes from real reviewer decisions already
present in the source data: clauses_batch_2.json carries a `review_history`
block with named reviewers, actions and notes. The auditor reads those
directly and compares them to what the agents concluded.
This file adds what the source data cannot supply: batch 1 (API v2.1) has no
review_history field at all, so there are no recorded human decisions for
any of its 12 clauses. The entries below stand in for reviews that would
exist in a real deployment, and every one is marked source='simulated' in
the ledger so it can never be mistaken for a genuine reviewer record.
In production this file does not exist. Overrides arrive from the review UI
IMPORTANT: an override changes the outcome for ONE clause. It does not
change a threshold, a prompt, or a rule. Only an approved learning proposal

reviews.rationale: Agreed. Indemnifying the Owner for its own negligence is uninsurable under our professional liability policy. This is the clause that drove the Section 8.1 amendment.
reviews.note: Confirms the agent rather than overriding it. Recorded because agreement is evidence too -- a ledger that only captures disagreement overstates the error rate.

reviews.rationale: Duty to defend is non-negotiable on federal work and is priced into the fee. Accepting it here rather than treating it as a breach of standard.
reviews.note: Second override on the same standard. Two occurrences is what triggers a learning proposal -- see agents.auditor.min_occurrences_for_proposal.

reviews.rationale: Discretionary withholding is the real problem here, not the 60-day term. Escalating to the client's counsel.
